newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's BNI bank plans global roadshow.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's BNI bank plans global roadshow.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned PT Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) said on Wednesday it planned a roadshow to Japan, Europe and the United States ahead of its listing on the Jakarta Stock Exchange later this year.
"We need to go to Japan, the U.S., and Europe. We need the long term investors from those countries," BNI president director Widigdo Sukarman told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
"We have almost concluded our preparations for the listing. We will able to implement the listing later this year," he said.
Sukarman declined to say how much of the bank's equity will be floated or what the proceeds will be.
"BNI's move to go public is to achieve capital adequacy ratio of 12 percent in the year 2001," he said. He gave no other details.
BNI, Indonesia's largest state-owned bank, posted a gross profit of 401.1 billion rupiah in 1995 against 308.1 billion in 1994.
